episode.title: Recognize an official model alias when resolving context and output budgets
episode.before: At parent commit 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe, the ordered input-limit table recognized only names beginning with `deepseek-v4` as the 1,000,000-token tier. The official `deepseek-flash` name therefore matched the later generic `deepseek` rule and resolved to 131,072 input tokens. The output table likewise recognized only `deepseek-v4`; because `deepseek-flash` matched no output-specific rule, `tokenLimit(..., 'output')` returned the 32,000-token default. Existing tests covered V4-prefixed and older-family names but not the official alias.
episode.after: At commit 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864, both ordered tables recognize names beginning with either `deepseek-v4` or `deepseek-flash` before their generic fallbacks. Consequently, `deepseek-flash` resolves to a 1,000,000-token input context and a 384,000-token output limit, while older DeepSeek families retain their existing 128K input and family-specific/default output behavior. A focused regression test asserts both limits for the official alias.
episode.diff: The change replaces `/^deepseek-v4/` with `/^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)/` in the input and output limit tables, adds comments explaining the official-name alias and ordered-fallback hazard, and adds two regression assertions for `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash')` and `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash', 'output')`. No normalization, compaction algorithm, or generic fallback values were changed.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864 is the implementation-bearing resolution linked to issue 11894 through PR 11909; its parent is 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe and it changes only the token-limit implementation and its unit test.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json fields resolved_commit, parent_commit, linked_pull_requests, commit_show_stat, and changed_files_name_status; local `git show --stat 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864`

evidence_units.claim: In the parent implementation, the specific input rule `/^deepseek-v4/` mapped to 1,000,000 tokens and preceded the generic `/^deepseek/` rule mapped to 131,072 tokens, so normalized `deepseek-flash` selected the generic 128K rule.
evidence_units.source: `git show 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts`, PATTERNS DeepSeek section and first-match `findTokenLimit` loop

evidence_units.claim: In the parent output table, only `/^deepseek-v4/` mapped to 384,000 tokens; `deepseek-flash` matched none of the listed DeepSeek output rules and therefore `tokenLimit` used DEFAULT_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT, whose value is 32,000.
evidence_units.source: `git show 156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts`, DEFAULT_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT, OUTPUT_PATTERNS, findTokenLimit, and tokenLimit

evidence_units.claim: The resolution broadens both the input and output V4-tier matchers from `/^deepseek-v4/` to `/^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)/`, keeping these specific rules ahead of generic family fallbacks.

The post-change comments state that the official API exposes V4 flash as `deepseek-flash`, that the alternative V4.1 spelling belongs to another endpoint, and that the alias must not fall through to the 128K family rule.

`tokenLimit` normalizes the supplied model identifier, performs first-match lookup in the selected input or output table, and falls back to the corresponding default. Its contract documents that it is primarily used during configuration initialization to auto-detect context-window and output-generation limits.
evidence_units.source: `git show 3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts`, normalize, findTokenLimit, tokenLimit, and tokenLimit documentation

evidence_units.claim: The added regression test asserts that the official `deepseek-flash` name resolves to 1,000,000 input tokens and 384,000 output tokens.
Adjacent retained tests assert that V4-prefixed names still resolve to 1,000,000 input tokens and older names such as `deepseek-r1`, `deepseek-v3`, and `deepseek-chat` remain at 131,072 input tokens.

The commit message reports that the incorrect 128K/32K resolution caused long sessions to fail with `COMPRESSION_FAILED_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED` and states that the matcher expansion preserves older-family fallbacks.

candidate_workflows.description: When an accepted runtime identifier falls through an ordered capability table and produces undersized context or output budgets, identify both fallback paths, extend the narrow capability-tier matcher, and lock both lookup modes with regression coverage while preserving neighboring family mappings.

workflow_graph.goal: Make a supported official identifier resolve to its actual context-window and output-generation capacities without changing unrelated model-family budgets.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The identifier is accepted by the external service but is absent from the resolver's specific high-capacity matchers, causing ordered lookup to select generic/default budgets and destabilize long-session compaction.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Both input and output lookups classify the identifier at the intended capability tier, regression assertions enforce those values, and existing specific and generic family examples retain their prior mappings.
